newsitem.title: GERMANY: German plant breeders await French OK on gene maize.
newsitem.headline: German plant breeders await French OK on gene maize.

text.p: German plant breeders keenly await French authorisation of the marketing and cultivation of genetically modified maize in the European Union, Ferdinand Schmitz, managing director of industry federation BDP, said.
"We hope it will only be a matter of days," he told Reuters.
EU law requires that France, where the demand to allow transgenic maize on the EU market arose, should authorise the step after the EU Commission ruled in December that the maize was safe.
A French diplomat said on Wednesday the decision hinged on the industry's acceptance of a compulsary labelling code.
Schmitz said once gene modified maize developed by Swiss chemical firm Ciba Geigy AG has been cleared, some 10 to 15 other varieties may be presented for registration over the next two years.
They were being adjusted to suit different climatic conditions across the EU's geographically diverse growing regions.

Schmitz said BDP, which respresents some 100 small and medium-sized companies, was also aiming to obtain approval for genetically modified rapeseed with the aim of possible plantings in the 1998 winter for harvesting in 1999.

The Ciba corn, which has been made resistant to certain pesticides and the European corn borer, would be the first genetically modified crop grown in Europe, where environmental group Greenpeace is waging a war against transgenic crops.
An activist said on Tuesday the group would try and stop plantings of genetically modified maize on European soil while upholding its opposition to imported modified soybeans.
The crops may pose risks to human health and the environment, she said.
A farm union (DBV) source said even if the new maize was approved immediately, seed may arrive in the sales and distribution chains too late for April plantings this year.
